title: Supply Chain Visibility Platform
text: Shipment trackers are unreliable across the Middle East, so we built a cloud platform for logistics companies running import and export flows in the region. Iraq is the demo environment: simulated trucks move between Basra Port, Umm Qasr and depots in Baghdad, Mosul, Erbil and Kirkuk.

title: Supply Chain Visibility Platform
text:
Architecture

A Python simulator sends batches of shipment events to API Gateway
Lambda validates and normalizes each batch, writes it to DynamoDB, and archives the raw batch to S3
A Streamlit dashboard queries DynamoDB to show a live map, delivery-status breakdown and an active-shipments table
OSRM routing and distance-based ETA predictions flag detours and late deliveries

The full report covers data collection, cleaning, supervised and unsupervised analysis, and the AWS design.

title: What the Olive Trees Saw
text: A data-driven narrative about settlement expansion in the West Bank and its environmental and human impact. The project combines settlement footprints from Peace Now, event data from ACLED, and land use traced through OpenStreetMap and UN OCHA boundaries to test three claims: that expansion is continuous and increasing, that it grows close to Palestinian communities and farmland, and that olive groves sit at the intersection of it.

title: What the Olive Trees Saw
text:
What is in it

Territorial and heat maps of events against settlement growth
Settlement-proximity analysis for communities and agricultural land
Linked views connecting harvest-season targeting, perpetrators, damage types and fatalities
Before-and-after satellite comparisons of individual villages

It is a personal project as well as a technical one: the author’s family is Palestinian, and the harvest calendar is part of how they grew up.

title: The American Dream, Audited
text: A data-driven audit of what the American Dream actually paid out between 1960 and today, across three life stages and several demographic groups. Instead of treating the Dream as a sentiment, the project measures it in one unit: hours of full-time labor.

title: The American Dream, Audited
text:
Headline findings

The hours of labor needed to buy a house rose from 5,903 in 1970 to 11,823 in 2020, even for the white men at the center of the original promise.
Medical prices grew 2.4 times faster than the rest of consumer prices over the same window.
The Black household share of US net worth fell from 4.0% to 3.3% since 1989.
Black women’s life-expectancy gap with white women narrowed from 8 years in 1960 to under 3 years by 2017, the audit’s clearest case of a gap closing.

title: The American Dream, Audited
text:
How it was built
An idempotent five-stage pipeline (acquire, clean, analyze, build interactives, NLP) pulls from FRED, BLS, the US Census, NCES, CMS, CDC NCHS, the Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts and the UCSB American Presidency Project. Results are published as a scrollytelling Quarto site with interactive Plotly charts, and a text-analysis layer (sentence-transformers and BERTopic) examines how presidents talked about the Dream.

title: Basic RAG Pipeline
text: A retrieval-augmented generation pipeline over six synthetic shareholder letters, running entirely on a laptop. Documents are chunked, embedded with a local model, stored in a local Qdrant database, and queried by a local LLM, with no API keys and no cloud calls.

title: Basic RAG Pipeline
text:
What I explored

Answering: 12 year-specific questions answered from retrieved context.
Hallucination: prompts designed to push the model into inventing answers, and how grounding changes that.
Metadata: putting the year into the chunk text, then query rewriting, to fix retrieval that mixes up years.
Retrieval strategies: Qdrant payload filtering, MMR for diversity, and a BM25 plus vector hybrid, compared on the same questions.
Write-up: a hand-written explanation of RAG and a FAISS vs. Qdrant comparison.

title: ECG Arrhythmia Detection
text: We built and compared three deep-learning approaches for classifying heartbeats from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database into four classes: Normal, Supraventricular, Ventricular and Fusion. About 89% of beats are Normal, so models were selected on macro F1 rather than accuracy.

title: ECG Arrhythmia Detection
text:
Approach

250-sample windows around each R-peak, plus patient metadata and RR-interval features
Partial SMOTE oversampling of minority classes; four augmentations for the hybrid model
CNN baseline on 64x64 log-magnitude STFT spectrograms
Transformer baseline on z-scored raw waveforms with patch embedding
Hybrid: pretrained EfficientNet-B0 patch tokens plus a metadata token fed to a Transformer encoder
Random hyperparameter search (15 configurations) per model

title: Hardening and Modernizing FMBench
text: FMBench is an AWS tool that benchmarks foundation models across SageMaker, Bedrock, EKS and EC2. The constraint of this assignment: the pipeline cannot be run (it needs AWS infrastructure, quota and spend), so every change had to be made and verified without executing it. I used coding agents for the heavy lifting and treated verifying their work as the main skill.

title: Hardening and Modernizing FMBench
text:
What I did

Understood it: wrote an explainer, module map and architecture diagram, and recorded where the AI’s first reading of the code was wrong and how I caught it.
Hardened it: wrote 138 characterization tests, configured ruff, bandit, mypy and pytest, and triaged every bandit finding by hand with a verdict and justification.
De-notebooked it: its production pipeline was seven Jupyter notebooks executed by papermill. I made the case against that design and replaced the runner with a plain orchestrator, converting two notebooks, backed by stubbed unit tests and a call-sequence golden master.
Cross-checked it: had a second model review the refactor and adjudicated its findings against a rubric.

title: Predicting Refugee Influx
text: We built a country-year panel (170 countries, 4,929 observations, 1992-2024) from UNHCR, UCDP conflict data, World Bank indicators and the Dataset of World Refugee and Asylum Policies (DWRAP), then predicted which countries see a surge in refugee inflows. Neighbor-aggregated features capture conflict and policy in bordering countries.

title: Predicting Refugee Influx
text:
Method

Target: top-quartile year-over-year log change in refugees hosted
Temporal split: train on 1992-2019, evaluate on a 2020-2024 holdout
Four models: logistic regression, XGBoost, XGBoost with geography, XGBoost with policy

title: Predicting Refugee Influx
text:
Findings

Holdout ROC-AUC rose from 0.793 (logistic regression) to 0.839 (XGBoost with the 12 policy indices)
No conflict feature reached the top ten by permutation importance, since lagged refugee counts already absorb recent conflict
The model under-predicts sudden shocks such as Syria 2015, Afghanistan 2021 and Ukraine 2022
